adaptations.reason: The checked-in corpus is German because the novel is written in German first and the notes are the author's working material; the prose in 08 Writing is the product itself. L1's one-language requirement therefore applies to the steering artifacts (CLAUDE.md, README.md, .github/, 10 Method/), which are American English. The German corpus is deliberately NOT in ignore, so the link and withdrawn-rule scans keep covering all 144 files; measured 2026-08-06, the whole vault corpus produces four spelling findings under american, all the single word Analyse, which is allow-listed together with Paralyse; a fifth occurrence comes from the method-log entry that names the word, which is recorded there so a later count of five does not read as drift. What is narrowed is the meaning of a clean run: the spelling scan proves nothing over German prose, because it compares it against English word pairs it never meets there. The same holds for the five German procedures under .claude/skills/.

There is no branch protection and no ruleset on main (decided 2026-08-06, deliberately). The review boundary exists as a way of working, not as a setting: the agent commits to a branch, opens a pull request and stops; merging is done by hand. What is missing is named rather than hidden - a push straight to main is technically possible and nothing prevents it, not even by accident. To change that, configure a ruleset at https://github.com/nanatsusaya/lumora/settings/rules with required approving reviews = 0, because most platforms forbid approving your own pull request and a higher number would make the trunk unmergeable for a single-author project.
